blindSummary:
This country carries severe risk for transgender visitors. A penal-code provision criminalises same-sex "indecent acts" (6 months-3 years), and rights documentation shows trans people facing de-facto criminalisation under a separate morality provision - arrests based on gender-expression discrepancies and forced outing. A 2026 rights report describes a legal-medical-social system of erasure for trans people, including a de facto prohibition on transition care.

Visitor-relevant cases exist: in 2024, a foreign social-media influencer was arrested in a major tourist city, accused by police of being transgender, and alleges she was forced to show her genitals - she spent a month in jail. In 2019, police in the same city filmed and humiliated a cross-dressing man after a traffic accident, leaking the video online. There is no legal gender recognition framework and police have wide discretion; the big tourist areas are more tolerant in practice but the legal exposure is constant.

The 2024 case demonstrates that even a cisgender visitor suspected of being trans can face genital inspection and jail.
blindOutOfScope: Same-sex criminalisation is a situational/climate factor; the 2024 arrest of the foreign influencer was officially for filming a policeman - the trans-suspicion genital inspection is her allegation, disputed by the authorities.
blindSourceSummaries: Human-rights report on the systemic erasure of transgender people in this country (Jan 2026): based on interviews with 17 trans and non-binary residents - documents an interlocking system of legal, medical, social and economic hostility; this country once pioneered gender-affirming surgery for foreigners but now enforces a de facto prohibition for its own citizens; the indecent-acts provision is weaponised to arrest trans people based on gender expression; no legal gender recognition pathway.

Rights-group country review: no specific provisions on transition, but de facto criminalisation under the morality provision (moral charges, gender-expression discrepancies, involuntary outing); no gender-affirming healthcare framework, leading some to self-medicate; a 2021 recognition process exists for intersex people only; the top official religious authority opposes transition.
Foreign daily (Nov 2024): a social-media model alleges police forced her to show her genitals over trans suspicions - reported police abuse of a trans woman based on appearance.

Foreign broadsheet (Jan 2019): police subjected a cross-dresser in a tourist city to online humiliation - after a minor traffic accident, he was handcuffed and filmed by bystanders and police officers, who also photographed his ID documents and posted them online; he later sought asylum abroad. Homosexuality is punishable in this country.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): the penal code criminalises 'indecent acts' between persons of the same sex (6 months to 3 years) with wide police discretion and arbitrary arrests; 170 people charged with same-sex relations in 2018; an international human-rights organisation documented a 2020 campaign of online harassment of presumed gay and bisexual men; no legal gender recognition; public identification as LGBTIQ carries significant risk of violence and harassment; authorities block LGBTIQ organisations.

International human-rights organisation report (April 2018) on LGBT activism in the face of adversity: includes this country's criminalisation of same-sex conduct and an annex of laws used across the surrounding region to punish same-sex conduct and gender expression.
International LGBTI association's world legal survey (May 2008) of laws prohibiting same-sex activity between consenting adults - country-by-country legal survey including this country.
Overseas LGBT community newspaper (Sept 2014): the UN Human Rights Council adopted the SOGI resolution - international context for human-rights scrutiny of countries including this country.
blindLocalsOnly: The de facto transition-care prohibition described in the 2026 rights report is resident-facing.
blindTangential: A penal-code provision criminalises same-sex "indecent acts" (6 months-3 years) - a direct risk for trans visitors with partners.
